Heard from the TV: "A new friend from abroad asks how you practise English. Compare watching YouTube with listening to music for learning English, and give two reasons for your choice."
steps.thought: Fine, I'll compare them and give two reasons.

args.text: I think YouTube is better for learning English than just listening to music. Firstly, you can see the person speaking and often turn on subtitles, so it is easier to connect the words with the pronunciation. Secondly, YouTube videos use normal everyday language, while songs often have unclear lyrics and slang. On the other hand, music is good for relaxing and remembering some phrases, but I learn more from videos.

Heard from the TV: "Your friend says gaming is a waste of time if you want to study abroad. How would you respond? Argue your side, and admit one point where your friend might be right."
steps.thought: Fair question; I'll argue gaming helps but admit the time-wasting risk.

args.text: I don't agree that gaming is a waste of time. When I play with people from other countries I must communicate in English quickly, so I learn new words and I am not afraid to speak. Also many games have a lot of story and dialogue, which is good listening practice. However, my friend is right in one point: if somebody plays ten hours a day, he has no time for real studying and his grades can suffer. So it depends on how much you play, not on gaming itself.

judge.voice: Honestly, B2 feels right, and it took one sitting, so I'd use it again before the interview. The tasks were about gaming and YouTube, not baby stuff, which I liked. The "right in one point" catch was real and useful. But the summary felt thin: "everyday talks abroad are within reach" sounds like a template, and I wanted more than one fix. It also said it placed me a level lower "to be safe", which is odd when my answers were "nearly there" for C1. Praise like "Nice work" had little content. I'd trust the level more with a clear reason and a short list of my usual slips. Compared with a 4,000 CZK course it's a decent quick check, and I'd mention it to classmates, with the warning that the plan part is light.
